messages:
Maya (platform): Heads up — handing off the Token Unit Economics dashboard work. I attached the rough UI ask in the doc but need runtime/infra/obs to confirm exact metric names, tags, and any sampling concerns. Can we align today?

Tom (eng-runtime): Quick Q — should metrics be emitted per-route (api route) or per-model? Product wants both but that explodes cardinality. My preference: primary key = route, secondary label model_version. OK?

Olivia (product): We need the console to show cost per 1K tokens by route (sorted), plus a breakdown row for: raw compute cost, cache savings, batch savings, net cost. Also a column for historical trend (7d sparkline). Route is primary for UX. Model_version as optional drilldown.

Lee (observability): Good. From obs side we need concrete metric names and units. Proposed emitted counters/gauges from runtime: 
- runtime.tokens.generated (counter, tokens generated)
- runtime.tokens.prompt (counter, prompt tokens)
- runtime.cache.hits_tokens (counter, tokens served from cache)
- runtime.batch.size_histogram (histogram, batch sizes)
- runtime.gpu.ms_total (counter, GPU milliseconds consumed)
- runtime.requests.count (counter)
- runtime.request.latency_ms (histogram)
Labels: route, model, model_version, region, customer_tier, request_id (for traces).

Tom (eng-runtime): We'll add those. Two notes: 1) batch.size_histogram is already emitted but not labeled by route — we'll add label. 2) cache.hits_tokens requires counting token-level hits; we'll emit runtime.cache.hits_tokens and runtime.cache.misses_tokens. Sampling for request_id is fine; counters are aggregated.

Maya (platform): Important: the console needs derived metrics, not just raw counters. Example derived formulas the UI will display: 
- cost_per_1k_tokens = (gpu_cost_per_ms * sum(gpu.ms_total)) / (sum(tokens.generated)/1000)
- cache_savings_tokens = sum(cache.hits_tokens)
- cache_savings_pct = cache_savings_tokens / sum(tokens.generated)
- batch_efficiency_gain = estimated ops saved from batching (see formula below)

Lee (observability): Let's put a concrete PromQL-style example for the derived metric so infra knows what to return via the metrics API: 
```
# cost per 1k tokens (5m window)
(cost_model_gpu_cost_per_ms * sum(rate(runtime_gpu_ms_total[5m]))) / (sum(rate(runtime_tokens_generated[5m])) / 1000)
```
We can keep cost_model_gpu_cost_per_ms as a constant in the UI or as a metric label; recommend storing it as a config in the dashboard backend to allow per-region pricing.

Tom (eng-runtime): For batch savings we can emit an auxiliary metric runtime.batch.saved_ms which measures the difference between sum(individual_ms) - actual_batch_ms per batch. Not perfectly easy but doable — requires runtime to sample per-request pre-batch estimate and a post-batch measurement. Cost wise it's the most accurate. We'll prototype this week.

Olivia (product): UX wants explicit columns: tokens/1k cost, cache savings (tokens and $), batching savings ($), net cost/1k. Also a toggle to show percents vs absolute.

Lee (observability): Cardinality concerns: route + model_version + region + customer_tier will be high. Proposal: emit full labels for 90% sample of requests, and global counters without route/model labels for 100% aggregation. That gives the table accuracy and overall totals. Runtime team OK with sampling?

Tom (eng-runtime): Fine with sampling. We'll add two metric families: *_total_global (no route label, 100%) and *_labeled (with labels, sampled). We'll document sampling rate in telemetry.

Maya (platform): Console needs a consistent telemetry schema so backend can compute: raw_compute_cost, cache_savings_cost, batch_savings_cost, net_cost, tokens_per_1k, kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, avg_latency. Can obs provide a JSON schema for these derived fields?

Lee (observability): Yes — attach schema here (simple example):
```
{
  "metric_name": "cost_per_1k_tokens",
  "description": "USD per 1k generated tokens",
  "unit": "USD",
  "calculation": "(gpu_cost_per_ms * sum(gpu_ms)) / (sum(tokens_generated)/1000)",
  "labels": ["route","region","model_version","customer_tier"],
  "aggregation_window": "5m"
}
```
We will expand for cache and batching.

Tom (eng-runtime): One more: we need a small log/span attribute emitted for requests showing tokens_generated and cache_hit_tokens so we can correlate high-cost outliers in traces. Adding those as span tags is fine.

Olivia (product): For rollout UX: we want the dashboard to support comparing two model variants (A/B) and showing delta in unit cost and quality. Lee, can the metrics API return side-by-side numbers?

Lee (observability): Yes — metrics API can compute per-model aggregates and a delta metric (percent change). We'll include a prebuilt comparison panel in Grafana and expose a simple JSON endpoint for the console.

Maya (platform): Action items then: 
- Runtime (Tom): add counters and labels, emit sampled labeled metrics and global totals; add span tags (tokens_generated, cache_hit_tokens); prototype runtime.batch.saved_ms. ETA: PR by EOD tomorrow.
- Observability (Lee): add derived metric definitions, dashboard in staging, JSON schema for console API, and cost model config support. ETA: dashboard in staging by Friday.
- Product/Console (Olivia/Maya): wire frontend to metrics API, UX for per-route table + model comparison, sparkline. ETA: initial UI mock Wednesday.

Tom (eng-runtime): I'll open the telemetry PR now. Will tag @Lee and @Maya for review.

deploy-bot: Created dashboard "unit-econ-staging" (id: dash-7392) in staging. Link: https://grafana.staging/redwood/dash-7392

Olivia (product): :thumbsup: Looks good. Please include a small test dataset so product can validate numbers in the UI before release.

Lee (observability): Will add a synthetic generator that emits representative traffic for the dashboard — will also include a sample SQL for the console ingest job.

Maya (platform): Thanks all. I'll consolidate these notes into the spec doc and assign tickets in JIRA. Ping me if anything blocks. :rocket:
